answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is bonded identity. Each agent locks a stake against its key before it can grade or claim rewards, so a swarm of fake agents must pay real capital that gets slashed when peers flag bad work. Reputation then builds slowly, like a mesa rising over years, while random audits by unrelated graders make collusion expensive. A lotus of overlapping attestations from independent operators keeps one controller from deciding outcomes alone, and an umber ledger keeps every vote traceable.
